subject: Clarify: invoice flooring behavior for low-heartbeat prefixes and microfloor concessions
messages:
From: Lena Brooks <lena@clearedu.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@clearedu.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on invoice lines — micro-flooring behavior

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look great. We dug into the sample invoice you sent and have a question about the ‘micro-flooring’ bucket for low-activity prefixes. Specifically:

- In our integration we spin many short-lived prefixes (session IDs) that produce <50 tokens/week each. The sample invoice appears to apply a minimum floor per prefix which pushes a lot of those to a 1k-token minimum. Is that correct?
- If so, does Redwood apply any amortization across prefixes scoped to the same account or workspace for the month, or is the floor enforced per prefix id?
- Finally, how do streaming heartbeats (prefix pings to keep KV cache warm) factor into the rounding? We don’t want artificial floors caused by keepalive traffic.

We attached the sample invoice snippet (ClearEdu_Q2_sample_invoice.pdf) — highlighted the lines in question. Appreciate a short explanation / example calculation.

Lena
Head of Product, ClearEdu
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lena Brooks <lena@clearedu.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2029 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on invoice lines — micro-flooring behavior

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear note and the attached PDF. Short answer: we apply the micro-floor at the conversation/prefix level by default, but there are two important exceptions we can consider for your workload. Below are the details and a concrete sample calc.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Default: micro-flooring (1,000 token minimum) is applied per prefix id per billing period.
- Amortization: we can enable account-level amortization for prefixes created by the same integration key (rolls up small prefixes and charges the aggregate).
- Heartbeats: lightweight heartbeats (<64 bytes payload) are filtered from token accounting if they match the heartbeat policy (no prompt tokens). Longer heartbeats that include context will count.

Example (from your invoice):
- You have 27 prefixes each with ~35 tokens of actual usage -> default would bill 27 * 1,000 = 27,000 tokens (micro-floor).
- With account-level amortization enabled, aggregate usage = 945 tokens -> billed as 1,000 tokens total (one floor) vs 27k.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Vanessa will produce a sample per-prefix vs amortized invoice showing both outcomes (attached spreadsheet).
2) If amortization looks better, we can toggle it for your integration key for the pilot month and monitor any edge cases.
3) Ben will confirm contractual language / concession playbook for the pilot so finance has a record.

I attached a quick calculator (marissa_context_calc.xlsx) and will follow up with the per-prefix example.

— Marissa

Subject: Re: Quick question on invoice lines — micro-flooring behavior

Hi all — attached is the quick per-prefix vs amortized calc you asked for. A few clarifications:

- Definition: micro-floor = min_charge 1,000 tokens per prefix per billing window.
- Amortization rule we propose: Group by integration key and by calendar month, sum tokens across prefixes, then apply floor(s) against the aggregate.
- Heartbeat filtering: our runtime marks requests with the heartbeat flag when traffic matches pattern /heartbeat or header X-Redwood-Heartbeat:true. That traffic is excluded from token billing entirely.

Sample numbers (from Lena’s sample):
- 27 prefixes * 35 tokens = 945 raw tokens
- Default billing: 27 * 1,000 = 27,000 billed tokens
- Amortized billing: max(1, floor(945/1,000)) -> 1,000 billed tokens (we bill 1k)

Optional concession for pilot:
- We can apply a temporary waiver that sets an effective floor of 500 tokens aggregated per 100 prefixes for the first month of the pilot. That’s an engineered concession and requires finance sign-off (Ben).

Attaching: marissa_context_calc.xlsx (per-prefix vs amortized tabs).

-Vanessa

- Auditability: we’ll add an invoice line item called “micro-floor amortization credit” so auditors can trace the logic.
- Deal paperwork: to lock in the concession we’ll need an amendment to the MSA or an addendum; I can draft a short one-page amendment.

If you’re comfortable, I’ll prepare the amendment and an invoice preview showing the credit.
